_instructions: B2 v2 scoring rubric. Renders use the tightened prompt constraints PLUS rule 5 (material + context baseline). Same scoring schema as B1.
_b2_prompt_changes_vs_b1: Added EXTRA CONSTRAINTS: 'The right facade has zero windows; do not add any. The corner is recessed, not wrapping — do not extend glazing around it. Mullion patterns must match the input exactly; do not invent new subdivisions. Window count per facade must equal what the input shows.'

Added rule 5: MATERIAL & CONTEXT BASELINE — neutral palette (light gray concrete/stucco walls, neutral glazing, dark mullions, gray concrete ground), single palette across all facades, no invented water features / skylines / vegetation.

failures.note: Corner wraparound — model ignored explicit constraint 'the corner is recessed, not wrapping'
Minor shape changes in distant/ambiguous regions
Some existing openings from source disappeared

nb_seed_42.notes: B1 had 2 critical (invention + corner). B2 reduced to 1 critical but corner still wraps despite explicit prompt constraint.

failures.note: Corner wraparound — REGRESSION vs B1 where corner was intact at this seed
Materials still drift but pool/skyline context inventions from B1 are gone

nb_seed_100.notes: Material baseline killed the pool + skyline inventions (huge win on context). BUT corner wraparound appeared at this seed for the first time — the geometry constraint may have introduced ambiguity that pushed the model toward wraparound.

failures.note: Some existing openings from source disappeared

nb_seed_200.notes: B1 had 2 critical (invention + transformation). B2 reduced to 1 critical (still corner) but photorealism jumped from 3 to 7.

failures.note: Right facade windows — REGRESSION vs B1 where this seed had zero critical failures
Materials drift from baseline (brick podium not in spec)

nb_seed_300.notes: REGRESSION. B1 seed 300 was the clean seed (0 critical, photoreal 7). B2 seed 300 invented right-facade windows the constraint explicitly forbids. Seed lottery is no longer in our favor — the constraint changed the model's behavior in unpredictable ways.

deterministic_failures: Corner wraparound: now present in seeds 42, 100, 200 (3 of 4 seeds, up from 2 of 4 in B1). The explicit constraint 'the corner is recessed, not wrapping' did NOT stop the model. Soft prompt constraints are insufficient.

Right-facade window invention: persistent across seeds (was deterministic in B1, still present in seed 300 in B2). The explicit constraint 'right facade has zero windows; do not add any' did NOT stop the model.
stochastic_failures: Which seed maps to which critical failure flipped: B1 seed 300 was clean, B2 seed 300 invented windows. The constraint perturbed the model in unpredictable ways.
wins_from_rule_5_material_baseline: All B1 context inventions (swimming pool at seed 100, downtown skyline at seed 300) are GONE in B2.
Materials converged from wild variation (tan stucco / brick / white / cream) to a narrow neutral-gray-concrete range.
Photorealism improved on 2 of 4 seeds (100: 3→7, 200: 3→7). Other 2 seeds stayed at 5.
_summary.verdict_rationale: Nano Banana Pro cannot be prompted out of its core geometry hallucinations. The material+context baseline (rule 5) was a clear win on context inventions and material consistency, so rule 5 stays in the production prompt regardless of which renderer we pick. But geometry-pinning constraints are being treated as suggestions, not rules. We need a renderer that enforces edges as hard constraints — FLUX Canny Pro is the lead candidate because it uses Canny edges from the source as a ControlNet, not a prompt hint. Escalate to B3 bake-off.
